en.name: Youtiao (Chinese fried dough stick)
en.summary: Youtiao keeps 1–2 days loosely covered at room temperature, and 1 month at −18 °C (0 °F). Both figures come from the published timeline for doughnuts — in food-science terms the same thing, a lean fried dough — because no authority publishes one for youtiao.
en.pantry: 1–2 days loosely covered, and it is best eaten the morning it is fried. A sealed bag steams the crust soft within the hour, so leave it on a rack or in a loosely covered basket instead. Youtiao is a low-moisture fried dough rather than a perishable food, so what it does is go limp and then stale and rancid rather than turning dangerous, but in a warm humid kitchen it will eventually mould. If you have dipped it in soy milk or congee, that is a different situation and the leftovers do not keep.
en.fridge: No refrigerated timeline is published for youtiao, and the fridge is the wrong place for it. Chilling makes the dough stale faster — starch retrogradation runs quickest just above freezing — and the humidity of a fridge turns what remains of the crisp shell leathery. If you genuinely cannot eat it that day, the freezer does the job properly. Reheating a refrigerated youtiao in an oven does help, but it never comes back the way a frozen one does.
en.freezer: 1 month at −18 °C (0 °F). Bag it with the air pressed out and reheat in a hot oven or an air fryer — it crisps up noticeably better from frozen than from the fridge, because there is less free moisture to drive off. This figure is a conservative quality estimate on the same basis as the room-temperature one, not a published number. Kept continuously frozen it stays safe well beyond a month; the limit is the oil going rancid and freezer burn.
en.thawing: Do not thaw. Put it straight into a hot oven or air fryer from frozen; thawing first leaves it limp and oily.
spoilage: A limp, bendy stick that no longer crisps up in a hot oven.
A rancid, stale-oil or crayon-like smell — the usual end for a fried food.
Mould spots, which come quickly if it was bagged while still warm.
A dense, chewy interior instead of the open, hollow structure.
tips: Leave it uncovered or loosely covered; a sealed bag kills the crust in an hour.
Reheat in an oven or air fryer, never a microwave.
Freeze the surplus the morning you buy it rather than at the end of the day.
Day-old youtiao is excellent chopped into congee or fried rice, where limpness does not matter.

faq.a: 1–2 days loosely covered at room temperature, but it is at its best the morning it is fried. The figure is read across from doughnuts.
Yes, about 1 month at −18 °C (0 °F). Reheat straight from frozen in a hot oven or air fryer, which crisps it better than reheating from the fridge.

faq.q: How do you make youtiao crisp again?
faq.a: Dry heat — a hot oven or an air fryer. A microwave steams it and makes it chewy.

zh.name: 油條
zh.summary: 油條鬆鬆蓋著放室溫可放 1～2 天，−18 °C 冷凍是 1 個月。這兩個數字都來自甜甜圈的公布期限——從食品科學的角度看它們是同一種東西，都是油炸的瘦麵團——因為沒有權威機關為油條公布過數字。
zh.pantry: 鬆鬆蓋著、室溫 1～2 天，但最好還是炸好那個早上就吃掉。密封的袋子一小時內就會把外殼悶軟，所以請放在架子上或鬆鬆蓋著的籃子裡。油條是含水量低的炸物而不是易腐食品，所以它的結局是先軟掉、再走味油耗，而不是突然變危險；不過在又熱又濕的廚房裡，它終究會長霉。已經泡進豆漿或稀飯裡的那根是另一回事，剩下的不要留。
zh.fridge: 油條沒有公布的冷藏期限，而冷藏也不是它該去的地方。低溫會讓麵團老化得更快——澱粉回凝在略高於冰點時最快——而冰箱裡的濕氣會把僅存的酥殼變成皮革。如果真的當天吃不完，冷凍才是正確的解法。冰過的油條用烤箱回熱確實有幫助，但它永遠回不到冷凍那種程度。
zh.freezer: −18 °C 下 1 個月。壓出空氣裝袋，要吃時用高溫烤箱或氣炸鍋回熱——從冷凍回熱明顯比從冷藏回熱更酥，因為要趕走的自由水比較少。這個數字和室溫那個一樣，是保守的品質估計，不是公布的數據。只要全程沒退冰，放超過一個月仍然安全；限制它的是油脂油耗和凍燒。
zh.thawing: 不要解凍。直接從冷凍送進高溫烤箱或氣炸鍋；先解凍只會讓它軟塌又出油。
spoilage: 整根軟趴趴、可以彎折，進高溫烤箱也酥不起來。
聞得到油耗味、陳油味或蠟筆味——炸物最常見的結局。
長霉；還熱著就裝袋的特別快。
內部變得又密又韌，失去原本中空蓬鬆的結構。
tips: 不要蓋或只鬆鬆蓋著；密封袋一小時就能毀掉外殼。
回熱用烤箱或氣炸鍋，絕對不要微波。
多的請在買回來的那個早上就冷凍，不要等到晚上。
隔夜的油條切段丟進稀飯或炒飯非常好用，那裡不在乎它軟不軟。

faq.a: 鬆鬆蓋著放室溫 1～2 天，但最好吃的還是炸好那個早上。這個數字是比照甜甜圈而來。
可以，−18 °C 下大約 1 個月。直接從冷凍用高溫烤箱或氣炸鍋回熱，比從冷藏回熱酥得多。
用乾熱——高溫烤箱或氣炸鍋。微波只會把它蒸軟，變得黏牙。
